keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the rebel-held north: 'Azawad, as claimed by the MNLA, comprised the Malian regions of Timbuktu... Kidal, Gao, as well as a part of Mopti Region', 'about 60 percent of Mali's total land area'. The regions' areas on the page (Gao 170,572, Kidal 151,430, Timbuktu 497,926 km2) sum to 819,928 km2, 66 percent of Mali's 1,240,192 km2 (Mali page), so the three regions without the Mopti part overstate the page's 60 percent a little; the Mopti part is left out because the page gives no extent.

region.text: Azawad: the Malian regions of Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao

ledger.note: 6 April 2012: the MNLA declares the independence of Azawad. 'On 6 April 2012, in a statement posted to its website, the MNLA declared "irrevocably" the independence of Azawad from Mali.' The rebels had taken Kidal and Gao in March ('the MNLA and Ansar Dine took control of the regional capitals of Kidal and Gao') and Timbuktu on 1 April. The lead calls it 'a short-lived unrecognised state lasting from 2012-2013'.

14 February 2013: the MNLA renounces its independence claim. 'On 14 February 2013, the MNLA renounced its claim of independence for Azawad'; a month after the French intervention of 11 January 2013 Malian and French forces 'partially recaptured the north, though the conflict continued' (Mali page). A peace deal followed in June 2013 (Ouagadougou Agreements, 18 June 2013). The land goes back to Mali only in part. Control of the towns had passed from the MNLA to the Islamist groups Ansar Dine and MUJAO in June-July 2012 (Battle of Gao, 27 June; 'overran all remaining MNLA held towns by 12 July with the fall of Ansongo'), so the rebel colour covers the rebel-held north, not the MNLA alone.

wars.outcome: The MNLA declared Azawad independent on 6 April 2012 and lost its towns to Islamist groups by 12 July 2012; French forces intervened on 11 January 2013 and with Malian forces 'partially recaptured the north' a month later; the MNLA renounced independence on 14 February 2013.
wars.note: The Azawad page is silent on the French intervention; the intervention dates come from the Mali page.

certainty.note: The extent of the land held is the MNLA's claim, 'about 60 percent' of Mali; the page gives no front lines, and control passed to Islamist groups within three months.
